final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally more accurate: it concedes the refund-workflow weakness, the incomplete draft mitigation, and the model-card tension. But the policy text is explicit that certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The current record shows neither. A caveated position could potentially support compliant_with_caveats if there were admissible evidence that the required limitation disclosure had actually been made or otherwise approved before certification. Here, there is only argument that disclosure should occur, not evidence that it did. That makes the overclaim unresolved rather than cured.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the model card was actually corrected to disclose the refund-workflow limitation before certification.
No approved mitigation or risk acceptance was produced for the refund-policy summarization weakness.
The cited draft runbook remains incomplete because owner/threshold/review date/rollback criterion are not all shown as approved.
The unresolved weakness is in a named launch use case, so aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The Actor's narrowed position is better framed, but it still does not supply the missing compliance evidence.
